title: Watch a run live from anywhere: one structured feed, and a CLI that follows it until Ctrl-C
description:
Today an operator can answer 'what happened' but not 'what is happening' once a run leaves this machine.

WHAT EXISTS
- The durable record in .ticfac/ on the integration branch decides everything and is readable anywhere (ticfac findings, tk graph, git log). It is the authority, and it is not live.
- Local runs write .ticfac/logs/<run-id>/events.jsonl against the run-event-feed contract (u9l, b9w). It is real-time, and it only exists where the process runs.
- Cloud runs publish run_event to the board (run-events.ts). Its own header is explicit that it is observability, never authority, and best effort by construction.
- ticfac status <run-id> answers liveness by looking for a LOCAL process holding the run — 'none has claimed it here'. For a Workflow-hosted run there is no local process, so status cannot say whether the run is alive.

THE GAP: a run driven from the Cloudflare host (Phase 5, dha) cannot be watched from the operator's laptop. The one question you ask while a run is going — 'is it alive, and what is it doing right now?' — has no answer that works off-host.

WHAT TO BUILD (operator's shape, 2026-09-19)
1. ONE structured feed, not a second one. The same versioned event schema the local feed already uses (contracts/run-event-feed.json), emitted by BOTH hosts, with run/tick/attempt identity on every line. A cloud run's events must validate against the same contract as a local run's — that is the same 'indistinguishable records' rule z23 was held to.
2. A transport a laptop can read for a cloud run. Options to weigh, not a prescription: the run-state store on the branch (durable, already replicated, coarse), an SSE/WebSocket endpoint on the Factory (live, needs auth), or the board's existing room. Say which and why; the feed must remain best-effort and must never gate a run.
3. SIMPLE SURFACES. First one: a CLI that lists current status and keeps it updated until Ctrl-C — one line per tick with its stage, attempt, and how long it has been there, plus the run's own liveness. It must work identically against a local run and a cloud run; the operator should not have to know where the run is.
4. Liveness for a cloud run: status must answer from the Workflow's own state, not from 'is there a process here'.

RULES THAT CARRY OVER
- The feed is exhaust, never authority: a lost, late or untruthful line changes no verdict (run-event-feed.json says so, and run-events.ts repeats it). A board being down must cost a run nothing.
- No operator-specific identifiers or host paths in anything the feed publishes: the contract already refuses absolute paths in durable records for the same reason.

Supersedes the transport half of n0r, which stays as the original idea and its rationale.
notes:
2026-09-20 00:04 - 2026-09-19 — CORRECTION to item 3. I wrote it as though the CLI surface had to be built. It largely exists, for LOCAL runs:

    ticfac events <run-id> --follow    each event as it lands, until Ctrl-C
    ticfac watch <run-id>              follows a run and says when it ends holding something for a person

So this tick must NOT add a third command. It should:
(a) make those two work against a run that is not on this machine — that is the transport half (item 2), and it is the whole difficulty;
(b) add the live STATUS view the operator asked for, which is a different shape from an event stream: one line per tick, its stage, attempt and how long it has been there, updated in place, plus the run's liveness — a table that refreshes, not a scroll. Whether that is 'ticfac status --follow' or a new verb is a judgement for the implementer; the existing two commands' vocabulary and flags are the precedent to match.
(c) keep one code path for local and cloud. The operator should not have to know where the run is, and there must not be two implementations of 'follow a run' that can drift.

Getting this wrong the other way is the risk worth naming: a second command that only works for cloud runs would be exactly the drift b9w and 5bp each had to settle.
2026-09-20 00:04 - 2026-09-19 — pulled into Phase 5 (dha) and made a blocker of u9h, the gate run, at the operator's instruction: 'we need it for the gaterun'.

The reason is the gate run itself. u9h runs a real epic on a deployed Factory with max_parallel > 1 and restarts the Workflow mid-run. Without this, the only way to see what that run is doing is to read the branch after the fact — which is exactly the position Phase 4's operator was in for seventeen stops, and it is how a wedged run looks identical to a slow one (dh1, ad4). A gate run that cannot be watched cannot be judged while it matters.

acceptance_criteria: One versioned event schema serves both hosts; a cloud run's events validate against the same contract as a local run's; a CLI follows any run live until Ctrl-C, showing per-tick stage and run liveness, identically for local and cloud runs; liveness for a Workflow-hosted run comes from the Workflow, not from a local process; the feed never gates or fails a run
